goldens.comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.
goldens.reasoning: G1 says the test setup doesn't account for the new applyTemplateVariables(…, request.filters) call. C1 says the tests are inadequate because the mocked applyTemplateVariables hides the effect of the call, so it is a partial semantic overlap. C2–C4 are about the runtime bug where filters get duplicated, not the test setup.

candidates: Tests don't catch this bug because they mock datasource.runQuery so super.query() and its applyTemplateVariables call never execute, and the mock applyTemplateVariables does an idempotent string replace that hides the duplication

The new applyTemplateVariables call in runSplitQuery (line 298) causes ad-hoc filters to be duplicated on every split query, because DataSourceWithBackend.query() also calls applyTemplateVariables downstream, and addAdHocFilters unconditionally appends filter clauses without deduplication
For shard-split queries, applyTemplateVariables is called three times (runShardSplitQuery + runSplitQuery + DataSourceWithBackend.query), tripling the ad-hoc filters
The fix should remove the applyTemplateVariables call from runSplitQuery and runShardSplitQuery, relying solely on the existing call in DataSourceWithBackend.query()
